memory_update.text: BFAM should be tracked as a hidden employer-education-benefits platform via EdAssist, not just as an employer-sponsored childcare company.
STRA should be tracked for Workforce Edge employer-partner growth and whether employer benefits convert into lower-cost learner acquisition.
ATGE should be tracked as a healthcare-workforce pipeline asset where hospital/employer partnerships and clinical pathways may be the real chokepoint.
Employer-to-degree pipelines appear strongest where the employer has a hard labor shortage, especially healthcare, nursing, teaching, counseling, and regulated/licensed roles.
Need to verify which companies disclose actual employer-sourced starts, retention, graduation, and CAC advantage; partner counts alone are insufficient evidence.

summary: Expanded the universe around the hypothesis that employer, hospital, school-district, and institutional learner-sourcing networks may be a more defensible chokepoint than course content alone. The pass keeps Grand Canyon Education as the reference proof point and adds three US-listed underfollowed small/mid-cap candidates where the employer-to-education channel is either direct, embedded in benefits administration, or tied to healthcare workforce pipelines. This is a research universe only, not a recommendation.
